extracted.intended_audience: trademark examiners, national IP office classification staff, trademark searchers, and other persons responsible for coding figurative elements of marks
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory conventions for applying the Vienna Classification (5th Edition) to figurative elements of trademarks, including how to code, where to place elements, and administrative/depositary provisions of the Agreement. Intended to ensure consistent coding for effective anticipation searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature, languages and depositary functions (Article 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agreement shall be signed in a single original in the English and French languages, both texts being equally authentic. The original, when no longer open for signature, shall be deposited with the Director General. Official texts in other languages may be established by the Director General after consultation. The Director General shall transmit certified copies of the signed text and of any amendment, furnish certified copies of the Classification on request, register the Agreement with the UN Secretariat, and notify Governments of acts listed (signature, deposits of instruments, entry into force, declarations, withdrawals, acceptances of amendments, dates on which amendments enter into force, denunciations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative obligations and notification items are enumerated (i)–(x). Includes that both English and French texts are equally authentic and that certified copies/Classification copies will be furnished on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation and citation conventions for the Classification (Recommendations)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to write classification numbers and abbreviations: separate numbers of category and division, and of division and section, by a point; separate numbers of two different sections by a comma; use a dash to indicate an uninterrupted range of sections; if section numbers are not included, still separate category and division by a point; if several categories/divisions are necessary for one registration, indicate classification for every category/division separately in numerical order and separate these indications by a semicolon; indicate the edition by an Arabic numeral in round brackets (e.g., CFE (5)); the abbreviation to precede classification numbers is CFE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'CFE 3.9.10,24,25' for Category 3, Division 9, Sections 10, 24, 25; 'CFE 3.9.16-18' for Sections 16 to 18; 'CFE 1.1; 1.15; 2.9' when multiple divisions apply. Edition example: 'CFE (5)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Classification — facilitate anticipation searching
rubrics_metrics.description: The Classification's main purpose is to facilitate anticipation searching. For searching to be effective two operations must be completed: (i) consistent and correct classification (coding) of figurative elements to constitute the search file, taking future anticipating-search needs into account; (ii) correct definition of the sections in which prior marks have to be searched, taking coding characteristics into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These two operations are interdependent and should be entrusted to persons with proven skills in the trademark field who can assess figurative elements according to their distinguishing properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility and required skills for classifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification and definition of search sections must be entrusted to persons with proven skills in the trademark field; those persons should be able to assess figurative elements according to their distinguishing properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that coding decisions affect future searches — skilled personnel should make choices, implying quality/reliability is a criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: User preparation and mandatory reference materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Before using the Classification the user must familiarize themselves with the Preface (pages (v)–(viii)), the Recommendations of the Committee of Experts (page (xx)) and the General Notes (page 16). When using the Classification, the user should abide strictly by the Explanatory Notes and the references given in them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat Preface, Recommendations and General Notes as essential preparatory material; Explanatory Notes and cross-references are binding guidance for coding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of the Classification (three headings)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Classification is reproduced under three headings: (1) the Table of Categories (rapid guidance to categories); (2) the Table of Categories and Divisions, with Explanatory Notes (outline of divisions in a category to confine subject-matter); (3) the List of Categories, Divisions and Sections, with Explanatory Notes (complete information to decide final classification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory notes on a category apply to all its divisions even if not repeated; divisions are reproduced in the order of their categories, each followed by its sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auxiliary sections and coding convention for 'A' sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections with a letter 'A' before their numerical code are auxiliary sections that group figurative elements contained in main sections according to specific criteria. The letter 'A' should not appear in the numerical code assigned to the figurative element of a mark at the time of coding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections are for internal grouping; classifiers must code using the numeric code of the principal section (omit the 'A' in the recorded code).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples provided are informational only and not part of the Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The examples of figurative elements reproduced (pages 107–125) are given for information purposes only and therefore do not form an integral part of the Classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples may illustrate usage but do not override Explanatory Notes or sections — they are non-normative.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule: classify figurative elements by shape regardless of material or purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Figurative elements should be placed in categories/divisions/sections on the basis of their shape, regardless of material composition or the purpose of the object in which they are incorporated (e.g., toys shaped as dolls, animals or vehicles are placed in categories for human beings, animals and vehicles respectively).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material or intended function does not change classification — classify by visual/formal characteristics. Also: widely known pictures or sculptures should be placed in division 22.5 (if appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of an object forming part of another object
rubrics_metrics.description: The representation of an object forming part of another object should be classified under the same category/division/section as the object of which it forms part, unless expressly classified elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the bodywork of a motor vehicle is placed in sections 18.1.7 and A18.1.9 (as are motor vehicles), whereas tyres, wheels or steering wheel are placed in section 18.1.21 expressly intended for these parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous representations — place in multiple divisions/sections
rubrics_metrics.description: If a figurative element is presented so that it is not possible to determine clearly whether it belongs to a given division or section, it should be placed in both divisions or sections, unless there is a special note to the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a representation of a human being not clearly a man or a woman is placed in both divisions 2.1 and 2.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation similar to a listed item — place in that section even if not expressly mentioned
rubrics_metrics.description: The representation of an object or living creature similar to that of an object or living creature mentioned in the text of a given section is placed in that section even if it is not expressly mentioned there or in any other section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This supports flexible application of sections to near matches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marks with multiple figurative elements — classify each element separately
rubrics_metrics.description: If a mark comprises several figurative elements, each having its own distinctive characteristic and being classifiable in a different category/division/section, these figurative elements should be placed in the appropriate different categories/divisions/sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a bottle label with a castle and a characteristic form of writing is placed in the appropriate divisions/sections of categories 7 and 27; a man in uniform on horseback playing a trumpet is placed in sections 2.1.2, 2.1.20 and 2.1.9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of Categories — list and scope of Categories 1 to 29
rubrics_metrics.description: The Classification defines 29 categories that group figurative elements by broad subject-matter: 1 Celestial bodies, natural phenomena, geographical maps; 2 Human beings; 3 Animals; 4 Supernatural/fabulous/fantastic/unidentifiable beings; 5 Plants; 6 Landscapes; 7 Constructions/structures/advertisements/gates/barriers; 8 Foodstuffs; 9 Textiles/clothing/sewing accessories/headwear/footwear; 10 Tobacco/smokers’ requisites/matches/travel goods/fans/toilet articles; 11 Household utensils; 12 Furniture/sanitary installations; 13 Lighting/heating/cooking/refrigerating/washing/drying equipment; 14 Ironmongery/tools/ladders; 15 Machinery/motors/engines; 16 Telecommunications/sound recording/computers/photography/cinematography/optics; 17 Horological instruments/jewelry/weights/measures; 18 Transport/equipment for animals; 19 Containers/packing/representations of miscellaneous products; 20 Writing/drawing/painting materials/office requisites/stationery/booksellers’ goods; 21 Games/toys/sporting articles; 22 Musical instruments/accessories/bells/pictures/sculptures; 23 Arms/ammunition/armour; 24 Heraldry/coins/emblems/symbols; 25 Ornamental motifs/surfaces/backgrounds with ornaments; 26 Geometrical figures and solids; 27 Forms of writing/numerals; 28 Inscriptions in various characters; 29 Colours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each Category is subdivided into divisions and sections with Explanatory Notes; use the Table of Categories as rapid guidance to available categories when initiating classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division and section explanatory notes are binding for classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanatory Notes attached to divisions and sections explain inclusions, exclusions and cross-references (e.g., 'Note: Not including sparks (1.15.7) and asterisks (24.17.3)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classifiers must consult Explanatory Notes to resolve borderline cases, follow notes on exclusions/inclusions, and apply cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auxiliary sections content and association with principal sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Auxiliary sections list subgroupings associated with principal sections (e.g., A1.1.2 = one star, A1.1.3 = two stars). They are associated with specific principal sections and provide more granular distinctions for internal use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although auxiliary sections provide finer grouping, code assignments should use the principal numeric section code (omit the 'A' when assigning the code).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category/division-specific notes and examples should be followed
rubrics_metrics.description: Many categories/divisions include specific notes (inclusions, exclusions, examples), e.g., inscriptions representing a human being placed in 27.3.1; heads placed in divisions 2.1, 2.3, 2.5 or 2.7; 'Not including adolescent' note etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow category/division notes to avoid misclassification (these notes can override general instincts about placement).
